function.name: give_up
function.arguments: {"reason": "Could not complete the pick-and-place within the remaining decision budget. The wrist-view geometry misled my first block estimate; my descents nudged the block progressively +x/+y (it ended near +0.06,+0.055 per the fixed cameras, versus -0.07,-0.02 at trial start). Two grasp attempts closed on empty air, and then the gripper stopped responding to open commands: three consecutive move_to calls with gripper=1 were truncated to 1-3 control steps with the measured opening stuck at 0.013, leaving the jaws closed at 2.6cm, too narrow for the 4cm block. With two decisions left there is no way to reopen, grasp, carry, and place.", "hindsight": "1) The wrist camera is not a straight-down view: it looks diagonally ahead/down, so treating wrist images as a top-down pinhole camera gave block positions wrong by several cm; measure object offsets relative to a known landmark (the bowl) in the fixed front/side cameras instead. Front camera image-right is +x, side camera image-right is +y; the bowl center is near (-0.005,-0.036). 2) Position-only move_to commands execute only ~0.1-0.2s (1-2 steps, about 1cm) per submission; commands that include a gripper state change execute the full ~80-step interpolation so the arm converges completely - bundle repositioning with gripper toggles early, but after several rapid gripper commands the open command started being truncated to 1-3 steps with the jaws never opening, so do not rely on it late. 3) The jaw gap runs along world x at yaw 0 and the workable grasp height is z~0.85; descending pads easily nudge the block +x/+y, so re-verify the block position after every failed grasp before closing again."}
